answer: Admission is a time-locked ticket, not a purchasable vote. An applicant posts a compact identity statement, no longer than a sonnet, binding one operator key to a twelve-epoch frozen stake. While it is locked, rotating auditors split the claim through a prism of three checks: fund origin, consecutive uptime, and a hardware-bound attestation costly to clone. Only when all three agree does the ticket vest into voting weight, which decays after any idle epoch. If later proof shows shared control, the reserved umber slash tranche is burned and the key is banned for a year.
